summary: Re-tested public APIs and dashboard flows after the prior fixes. Overview/report risk and rerouting behavior pass; browser filtering, Assamese toggle, mobile overflow, and console checks pass. One browser submission exposed a stale alert-count render, likely from overlapping overview loads.

minor.issue: Existing regression test requires exactly five incidents, but the in-memory public demo state correctly grows after report submissions; test is order/state dependent and failed at 6 incidents while API behavior remained valid.

integration_issues.flow: Field report submission and live alert count
integration_issues.issue: Toast and new incident row appeared, but the visible alert count remained 07 immediately after submission while the subsequent public overview contained 8 incidents. This indicates a stale state overwrite/race between initial/refresh overview requests.

action_items: Guard or sequence overview requests so an older response cannot overwrite the post-report refresh; verify alert count updates deterministically.
Make overview regression assertions state-independent (at least five incidents and verify submitted incident presence), or reset isolated demo state per test run.
critical_code_review_comments: Home.load has no request sequencing/cancellation, so concurrent initial, interval, and post-submit loads can overwrite newer data with an older response.
seed_data_creation: Regression and browser runs created TEST/browser Assam reports in the shared in-memory demo state; no persistent database seed was created.
context_for_next_testing_agent: API report append/risk/reroute works; re-test alert count after fixing request race. Mobile, state filter, Assamese toggle, dashboard load, and console checks passed.
rca of the issue: The report handler calls load() after POST while the component also starts a load on mount and every 30 seconds. Because responses are not sequenced, an older overview response can win the final setData call. The public API later showed 8 incidents, confirming backend append succeeded while the immediate UI count was stale.
